name: Citalopram
summary: A highly selective SSRI that is simple to dose; QT prolongation is the main dose-limiting concern, capped at 40 mg/day.
mechanism: Highly selective inhibition of serotonin reuptake via SERT.

pharmacokinetics.elimination: Renal (partly unchanged drug) plus hepatic metabolism

dosing.adult: 20 mg once daily; may increase after 1–2 weeks

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; among the better-studied SSRIs in pregnancy — weigh against untreated depression.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; generally considered compatible with monitoring.
contraindications: Known QT prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Dose-dependent QT prolongation — cap at 40 mg/day; caution with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
monitoring: Mood and suicidality early in treatment
ECG and electrolytes in patients at QT risk
safety.overdose: Overdose can cause QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, and seizures — cardiac monitoring warranted.

indications: Off-label: generalized anxiety, panic disorder, OCD
clinicalPearls: Most selective SSRI with a relatively clean interaction profile — but the QT effect caps the dose at 40 mg.
CYP2C19 poor metabolizers or interacting drugs can raise levels — watch for excessive sedation.
good: Straightforward depression where a highly selective, interaction-light SSRI is wanted.
bad: Patients with QT risk factors, electrolyte disturbance, or other QT-prolonging drugs.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard psychopharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
